text: Every bank in the European Union must be able to pull an I.C.T. service back in-house. That is DORA Article 28(8). Proving it means reading every supplier contract for an exit clause, an audit right, a way to get your data back. Nobody does, because there are hundreds. This is Nordhafen's register: sixteen contracts, and seven million euros a year running through arrangements the bank cannot cleanly exit.

The core banking platform. Fourteen of the fifteen provisions Article 30 requires are present. This is a good contract. The one it lacks is the exit strategy, so the exit plan for the bank's most critical system cannot actually be executed. Every tick is backed by the clause it came from. No quote, no claim.

That was the bank's own paper. This one is real: an agreement filed with the S.E.C. by people who had no idea what we would check. A hundred and thirteen thousand characters. Far too long to read in one pass, and truncating it would lose the middle, where the operative clauses live. So the contract is split into passages and vector-searched against itself. The agent read eleven of them.

Castellan Core Systems. The supplier runs its own annual penetration test and will not let the bank test production. The checklist calls that a gap to close. A third-party risk officer would call it a stop. So the reviewer disagrees, and writes one sentence explaining why. It is embedded on the box and written to MongoDB. Nothing is retrained.

The agent is subscribed to that collection. It woke up on its own, and re-checked all sixteen contracts in under two seconds. It re-read nothing. Which clauses a contract contains had not changed. Only what the bank makes of them had.

This is everything the agent knows that is not in the code. Thirteen rules, each one a sentence a named person wrote, sitting next to the contract that prompted it. You can read all of it, and you can switch any of it off.

Now the part that matters. Aurora K.Y.C. Nobody opened this contract. It has the same weakness, so the agent found the rule by meaning and applied it here too, at a similarity of nought point eight six. On a contract that does have a testing clause, the same rule was retrieved, and correctly withheld.

One MongoDB does three jobs here: the register, the vector store, and the change streams that keep the agent awake. Rules open nothing. Retrieval grounds everything. A human decides. And all of it runs on hardware in the building. Unplug the network, and the thing that proves you could leave a provider carries on working.
